title: 4 Controversial Tips to Improve Your Communication
summary: The creator shares four unconventional hot takes to help you become a better speaker and communicator faster than traditional advice. Instead of looking in a mirror or reading books alone, she advises putting yourself out of your comfort zone, watching TV series and movies, copying three distinct internet personalities, and recording yourself on camera daily.
key_points: Deliberately put yourself in high-fear situations, like talking to someone out of your league, so that job interviews, boss interactions, and dates feel less intimidating.
Watch series and movies instead of just reading books to observe lip movement, facial expressions, body language, and vocal emphasis.
Pick three internet personalities whose speaking style you love, and practice speaking like them to develop your unique style.
Be the 'annoying wannabe' who speaks English even if your friends talk in their native language.
Do not practice in front of a mirror; instead, record video of yourself every single day to track your progress and review your delivery.
content: Getting rejected by a tall and pretty  woman is how you become better at  communication. Honestly, I’m done  with a lot of BS advice on the internet  that, oh, stand in front of the mirror  and speak and that’s how you will  become a better speaker. Or, oh, go  read a lot of books and that’s how  you will become a better communicator.  All of that is BS to me. So I literally  sat down and I wrote all the hot takes  I have on how to become a better  speaker. But the first one that I want  to start with is: please go and talk to  a pretty and tall woman who is clearly  out of your league to be better at  communication. I basically mean when  you are talking to somebody. Who is  clearly out of your league, you are  going into fear mode. The next time you  are talking to your boss. Or you are  talking to your interviewer. Or you are  talking to your very pretty date. All  of these situations are obviously going  to activate the same fear in you. But  that fear will be nothing to you  because you have been rejected by so  many women. Who are out of your league.  And I kid you not. I have been in  Bangalore for the past some time now.  And I know a person here who once, when  I met him. He told me, "You know what?  Whenever I am in a pub or I am in a  cafe or whatever, I would deliberately  walk up to the most pretty woman and  ask her out because I know that she  most likely will say no, but I want to  take my shot." That—that’s the way  to do it. You have to go into fear mode  on purpose. Because you will go into  fear mode anyway. You will have to take  that interview anyway. You will have to  talk to your boss anyway. You will have  to go on a date anyway. So why not  activate fear mode on purpose and do  exactly what my friend did? Also, and  he is now a person who honestly gets  dates easily, who is honestly very good  at business. He is very social. I see  him at networking events all the time.  The second hot take is: watch series or  movies over reading books. Now don't  get me wrong. On my Instagram, I have  spoken a lot about a lot of  anti-brain-rot books. If you want to  check out those anti-brain-rot books,  it's also on my YouTube. You can go  check it out, like The Female Brain or  Marcus Aurelius 'Meditations, etcetera.  But when it comes to communication, I  always tell people that if you want to  speak better. Always watch something  instead of reading something. You know  why. Because when you read something,  you only get to know new words. I 100% agree. But when you watch something,  you see people saying the thing out  loud. You see their lip movement. You  see their feeling while saying it. You  read their body language. You read  their emotion and that is what you need  while you are trying to speak better as  compared to you sitting there and  reading a bunch of words. Reading is  going to help you only to the extent of  making you learn sentence structures or  vocabulary. But if you really want to  see how somebody is saying a word and  which feeling they are saying it with?  What is the emphasis they are putting  on which syllable? What is it they said  that made it look so cool and how you  can emulate it. All of that gets clear  once you watch a good series or movie.  My personal favorite is the one that is  Mad Men. So Mad Men is where there are  a bunch of men in the advertising space  and the way that these men speak is so  articulate because basically they have  to sell their ad ideas to the world.  And so when Don Draper speaks, I listen . I love Don Draper so much. And if you  do not have the time, just go and watch  Don Draper's 5-minute clips on YouTube  and you will see what I am talking  about. You will see just how charming  Don Draper is. I truly have a crush on  him. So go check him out. Number three  hot take is you do not have to find  your voice. Just copy someone. I know  this is the hottest take but just  listen to me. You know how people say,  just try to communicate, just speak  more and more, and you will find your  voice along the way. I 100%disagree  with that. Because what the person is  actually telling you is that throw  yourself into the fire. And we don't  know whether you are going to come out  of that fire and have a problem with  that. Because this is a very difficult  path to take. What you can do instead  is you can basically just copy someone.  Pick up three internet personalities.  Just three internet personalities whose  speaking style you love and just listen  to them. Just try to speak like them.  And once you copy these three internet  personalities you will basically become  like a product of the sum of these  three different personalities. And that  will still be better than who you are  today. And that is what I want. I don't  want to tell you, oh you know what,  stand in front of the mirror and  practice and you will be better. No, I  want improvement for you within like  two weeks, and how is that possible?  That is only possible once you sit down  and you have somebody actionable to  watch, you have somebody real to listen  to, and you have somebody you can  actually copy, like I have done it. I  openly say I used to watch a lot of  Whitney Cummings. And the way that I  have learned to speak, actually, is a  lot of this consuming Whitney Cummings.  And there is absolutely nothing wrong  with that. My ideas are original. My  love for my work is original. And if I  just see somebody speak and I want to  speak like them. I don't see why that  should be a problem. Next third take is  be that wannabe friend. Like just be  that wannabe friend who wants to speak  in English and who annoys the F out of  people because other people are like, " Why are you trying so hard to speak  English?" Like, we get it, dude. Just  be that person who is very annoying and  who is constantly trying to speak in  English. Because most likely you will  have people in your friend circle who  will be speaking in either Hindi or in  the native language. You, on the other  hand, want to improve your  communication. You want to speak better  English. So it's your responsibility  then to stand your ground and to speak  in English despite your friends  speaking in their language. Because  guess what, everything in your life  does depend on communication. You think  you are going to study hard and go to  that university and just crack the exam  and you are good. Absolutely no. You  will have to go through interviews. You  will have to go through GDs. What will  you do then? You will need  communication. But you just do not  practice communication with your  friends because they are going to laugh  at you. Like, how unserious is that?  Are you really going to throw your  career away because a bunch of people  are going to laugh at you? Who are also  19 years old, by the way, please do not  go by what 19-year-olds say. Please  have your own brain and practice  communication. Because trust me,  cracking exams is not enough. You also  have to be able to speak. If cracking  exams was enough. People would just  take your written exams and they would  be good to go, right? But that's not  how it works. You have to speak and you  have to let them know that you are an  intelligent being. But let's get to the  last hot take. Which is this. Do not  stand in front of the mirror and start  practicing communication. Nothing is  coming out of it. You know why? Because  there is simply no record of what you  said. There is usually no place where  you can go back and actually check what  you said, how you said it, how you  could improve, and what it is you have  to do in the future. What you really  need to do instead is pick up that  camera and record yourself. I cannot  emphasize this enough. I talk about it  all the time on my channel; I speak  about it on Instagram: pick up the  camera, record yourself, and talk about  your day. I need you to record a video  every single day and keep track of it.  See whether you did it every single day  or not. You know why? Because once you  have a recording, you have enough  evidence to go back to; you have enough  evidence to see how many times I am  stopping. How many times did I have to  take a retake? That's okay. I am not  telling you to post it anywhere. But  can you just pick up the camera and  record yourself every single day?  Please do it, and now that you have  stuck around in this video, think of me  as your accountability partner. What I  mean by that is, you know, my Instagram . Whenever you actually record yourself , just take a picture of your gallery,  blur everything else, and just send it  to me saying, "Hey Smriti, I heard you  and I think of you as my accountability  partner, and I just wanted to show you  that I actually did what you told me."  And if you see any progress, then also  do let me know because that makes me  really happy. I think recording myself  into the camera really made me  comfortable with who I am, how I look,  how I sound, etcetera. And I am pretty  sure it's going to help you too. So  that's it for today. But I really get  angry whenever I see bad advice on  communication on the internet. But I  will be coming up with more such videos  on communication. Now over to you, and  now it's your responsibility to tell me  in the comments as to what specifically  you need me to cover on communication.  Because I do see a lot of bad advice  floating around and I don't want that  for you. So go ahead, tell me, and I  will be happy to take that up. Until  next time, be a realistic optimist.
